sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is a font face? Mention any two font families.
questions.answer: A font face is the basic typeface (design of letters) in which text is displayed. Each family shapes letters in its own way. Examples: Times New Roman and Arial (also Calibri, Verdana).

questions.q: Differentiate between copying text and moving text.
questions.answer: Copying makes a copy of the selected text and puts it in another place, leaving the original unchanged (Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V). Moving (cutting) removes the selected text from its place and inserts it in another place (Ctrl+X, Ctrl+V).

or.q: Write the steps to move a line of text from one place to another.
or.answer: (1) Select the line of text. (2) Click Cut in Home → Clipboard or press Ctrl+X. (3) Place the cursor where the text should go. (4) Click Paste or press Ctrl+V. (Or drag the selection with the mouse and drop it in the new place.)

questions.q: What are headers and footers? How do you add them?
questions.answer: A header is text added to the top margin of every page, such as a title or page number; a footer is text added to the bottom margin. To add: Insert tab → Header (or Footer) → choose a style → type the text → close the header/footer.

questions.q: Write any two advantages of using the paragraph spacing command.
questions.answer: (1) Spacing before and after a paragraph does not change the size of the text, and precise adjustments can be made between headings and body text. (2) If the paragraph is moved or deleted its spacing goes with it, leaving no extra blank lines; spacing can also be included in styles.

questions.q: Differentiate between inserting a page break and deleting a page break.
questions.answer: Inserting a page break ends a page and starts the next one before the natural end: place the cursor and choose Insert → Page Break or press Ctrl+Enter. Deleting a page break removes a manual break: select the page break line (in Normal/Draft view) and press Delete.

questions.q: What is the use of the spell check feature in Word?
questions.answer: It finds spelling mistakes (red wavy lines) and grammar mistakes (green wavy lines). Press F7 to open the Spelling and Grammar dialog box and choose Ignore, Change, Change All or Add, so the document becomes correct without reading every word.

questions.q: Differentiate between a bulleted list and a numbered list.
questions.answer: A bulleted list marks each item with a symbol (bullet) and is used when the order does not matter. A numbered list marks items with numbers or letters in sequence and is used when order matters, such as steps of a procedure.

questions.q: Differentiate between portrait and landscape orientation of a page.
questions.answer: In portrait orientation (the default) the page is taller than it is wide; it is used for letters and most documents. In landscape orientation the page is wider than it is tall; it is used for wide tables, charts and certificates. Orientation is changed from Page Layout → Orientation.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Write the steps to set the tab stops in a paragraph.
questions.answer: (1) Select the paragraph. (2) Click the tab selector at the left end of the horizontal ruler until the required tab type (left, centre, right or decimal) appears. (3) Click on the ruler where the tab stop is needed. Or open Home → Paragraph dialog → Tabs, type the tab stop position, choose alignment and click Set/OK. Drag a marker to move it and drag it off the ruler to clear it.

questions.q: How do you set line spacing in a paragraph? What are the common line spacing values?
questions.answer: (1) Select the paragraph. (2) Home → Paragraph dialog launcher (or Line Spacing button). (3) In Indents and Spacing, choose Line spacing: Single, 1.5 lines, Double, etc., and click OK. Single spacing gives 12-point spacing, 1½ gives 18 points and double gives 24 points.

questions.q: Write the steps to make a centre-aligned paragraph in Arial right aligned (or justified) and in Times New Roman with double line spacing.
questions.answer: (1) Select the paragraph (triple-click). (2) Home → Font box → choose Times New Roman. (3) Click the Align Right button (Ctrl+R) or Justify (Ctrl+J). (4) Open the Line Spacing button or Paragraph dialog and choose 2.0 (Double). (5) Click outside to deselect.

questions.q: Write the steps to add page numbers to a document and start them from a chosen number.
questions.answer: (1) Insert tab → Page Number. (2) Choose Top of Page or Bottom of Page and a style. (3) To start from another number, choose Format Page Numbers. (4) In 'Start at', type the number. (5) Click OK.

questions.q: Write the steps to create a bulleted list and change its bullet symbol.
questions.answer: (1) Select the paragraphs, or place the cursor where the list should begin. (2) Home tab → Paragraph group → click the Bullets button. (3) To change the symbol, click the arrow next to Bullets and choose a bullet from the Bullet Library, or choose Define New Bullet → Symbol (or Picture), select one and click OK. (4) Press Enter after each item; press Enter twice to end the list.

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the steps for checking spelling and grammar in a Word document.
questions.answer: (1) Word underlines spelling errors with red and grammar errors with green wavy lines as you type. (2) Press F7 or choose Review → Spelling & Grammar. (3) The dialog box shows the first mistake. (4) If the word is correct, click Ignore, or Ignore All if it appears many times. (5) If wrong, choose a suggestion and click Change or Change All; or type the correct word. (6) Click Add for words like your name so they are not marked again. (7) For grammar, choose a suggestion and click Change or Ignore; untick Check Grammar to skip grammar.

or.q: Explain page formatting in Word: margins, paper size, orientation and page breaks.
or.answer: Margins: the space between the page edge and text; drag on the ruler or Page Layout → Margins (Normal, Narrow, Wide… or Custom). Paper size: Page Layout → Size → Letter, Legal, A4 or More Paper Sizes. Orientation: Page Layout → Orientation → Portrait or Landscape; it can be applied to selected pages. Page breaks: Word adds them automatically; insert one with Ctrl+Enter or Insert → Page Break; delete by selecting the break and pressing Delete.

questions.q: How do you create and format bulleted and numbered lists in Word?
questions.answer: (1) Click the Bullets or Numbering button on the Home tab. (2) Type the first item and press Enter for the next. (3) Press Shift+Enter for a new line without a bullet; press Enter twice to end the list. (4) Use Increase Indent to make a nested list. (5) Or type the text first, select it and click Bullets/Numbering. (6) To change the style, select the list, right-click → Bullets or Numbering (or Home → Paragraph) and choose a symbol, picture or number format, then click OK.
